case_studies.title: Evaluating LLM Trade-offs for Enterprise Automation: Lessons from Workflow Generation in a Production Enterprise Platform
case_studies.abstract: Enterprise compliance management requires rapid adaptation to evolving regulatory frameworks (e.g., DORA, AI RMF, FedRAMP) and tight remediation SLAs. Traditional static orchestrators often fail in hybrid cloud environments where event-driven assessments demand that automation code adapt to runtime context in seconds. This paper presents lessons learned from evaluating six large language models for AI-driven workflow generation in a production enterprise platform, benchmarked across 29 real-world IT automation scenarios, two generation pipeline architectures, and eight independent runs per pro
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of slow adaptation to changing regulatory frameworks in enterprise compliance management by building a system that uses large language models to generate workflows. The result is a more efficient and adaptable automation system. It benchmarks six large language models across various IT automation scenarios.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure with hybrid environments and event-driven assessments, here is what to do: review your current automation setup, consider integrating large language models for workflow generation, and assess the potential benefits for your specific use cases.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High IT relevance and novelty due to real-world evaluation of large language models in a production enterprise platform. Moderate value for 90 days due to lessons learned.

case_studies.title: FormBharo: Designing and Evaluating a Voice Agent for Conversational Form Filling in Rural India
case_studies.abstract: In India, almost every social benefit starts with a form, yet the people who need these benefits most are often unable to read or write. Reaching them requires a spoken conversation. Today that work falls to frontline health workers who enroll beneficiaries one at a time, a poor use of stretched capacity. We built FormBharo ("fill the form" in Hindi), a voice agent that fills a structured form over a phone call under tight latency and cost budgets by pairing Large Language Models (LLMs) with deterministic, rule-based validation and flow control. It is being piloted with ARMMAN, an NGO running
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of filling out forms for people who cannot read or write in rural India by building a voice agent called FormBharo. FormBharo is a system that fills out structured forms over a phone call using Large Language Models and rule-based validation. The result is a more efficient way to enroll beneficiaries for social benefits without relying on frontline health workers.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on a specific social benefit application in rural India, but IT consultants working with NGOs or similar organizations may find it relevant to explore for potential use cases.
case_studies.score_reasoning: While the paper describes a use case for LLMs, the focus on voice agents in rural India has limited novelty. The IT relevance and monetisation potential are moderate due to the application of LLMs and potential for service delivery.

case_studies.title: Post-Hoc Trajectory-Risk Certification for Modular LLM-Based Security Agents
case_studies.abstract: Autonomous security agents operate as staged pipelines, such as classifying network traffic and then attributing attacks to a specific technique. Split conformal prediction gives each stage finite-sample coverage, but deployment requires a trajectory-level guarantee across the full chain. These guarantees do not compose automatically when stages are independently trained and calibrated. Bonferroni allocation is distribution-free but conservative under correlated errors. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of guaranteeing the accuracy of autonomous security agents that operate in multiple stages, by creating a new method for certifying the reliability of these agents across all stages. The researchers built a new certification method that can be applied to existing security agents. The result is a more reliable way to ensure that security agents are working correctly.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud security infrastructure that uses autonomous security agents, here is what to do: review your current agent configuration to see if it uses staged pipelines, check if the current certification method is sufficient, and consider applying the new certification method to improve reliability. This flags a risk: if your org uses autonomous security agents with multiple stages, check the certification method immediately to ensure it is providing adequate guarantees. This is directly applicable to IT infrastructure work that involves cloud security.
case_studies.score_reasoning: High novelty and IT relevance with moderate AI maturity, but low potential for monetization. However, potential real-world impact is high.

case_studies.title: PLoRA: An NDP-Enhanced Pooled-Memory System for Cost-Efficient Multi-LoRA Serving
case_studies.abstract: Multi-LoRA serving is how one base model becomes thousands of specialized variants, one adapter per user, task, or agent, and the deployments can hold 1000-plus adapters. Serving them is hard because the workload inverts what GPUs provide: terabytes of memory against only tens of TFLOPS, and because every published system stages its adapters from CPU DRAM over PCIe, where each access pays a kernel stop and a host-run copy and capacity ends at the motherboard's DIMM slots. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of efficiently serving multiple specialized variants of a base model, known as multi-LoRA serving, by building a pooled-memory system called PLoRA. The result is a cost-efficient system that can handle thousands of adapters. This research aims to improve the performance of large-scale machine learning deployments.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage large-scale machine learning deployments, here is what to consider: review your current memory and storage infrastructure to see if a pooled-memory system like PLoRA could improve performance and reduce costs. Check if your organization's use of GPUs and CPU DRAM is optimized for multi-LoRA serving workloads. This may require re-evaluating your hardware and infrastructure to take advantage of memory-semantic fabrics like CXL and NVLink.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper discusses a technical improvement in LoRA serving. While novel, it's unlikely to have an immediate impact on the deployment aspect of LoRA. IT engineers might be interested in this improvement but it may not directly affect how they work daily. The information is not actionable enough for IT consultants to build, automate, or propose a service within 90 days.
